interac_context: In grandparent scams, fraudsters show up in person to pick up cash or request an e-transfer.
emerging_tactics: cryptocurrency investment fraud via social media

kill_chain_signals.contact: Fraudsters post ads on social media and lure investors through fake profiles on social media, dating websites, and email
kill_chain_signals.pretext: Fraudsters show up in person to pick-up cash or request an e-transfer in grandparent scam; victims offered job as financial receiver or agent
kill_chain_signals.payment: Victims are asked to deposit their funds into crypto accounts or wallets; fraudsters request cryptocurrency, e-transfer, or cash
kill_chain_signals.movement: Victims told to accept payments into their personal bank account, keep a portion, and forward the remaining amount to third parties
kill_chain_signals.cashout: Fraudsters attempt to process many payments in a short amount of time before the victim's financial institution recognizes the fraud

red_flags: Be careful when sending cryptocurrency; once the transaction is completed, it is unlikely to be reversed
If you receive funds from an unknown individual or company for any reason and are asked to forward it elsewhere - Don't!
If you are asked to boost apps, videos or merchandise, you will more than likely be providing fake reviews to fraudulent products
Never click on a link or attachment from an unsolicited message
If a caller claims to be a law enforcement official and asks you to pay a fine or bail, hang up and call your local police directly
key_quote: Specific scenarios may have evolved over time, but the underlying principles of exploiting emotions and urgency remain consistent.
title: Bulletin: Evolution of the types of fraud
